thread:
Anya: quick heads-up — noticed sampleapp surfaces inconsistent error objects between our SDKs. Customers see vague messages like 'ServerError' or '500' and it's blocking debugging.

MattG: can you show examples? which endpoints?

Anya: embeddings and generate. Python raises a ServerError with a tiny dict: {'code': 'server_error', 'message': 'internal error'}. JS just throws Error('500') with no structured fields.

Sarah-L: that's rough. We should converge on a minimal envelope across SDKs: code(enum), http_status, message, hint, retryable(bool), error_id. That would make UI copy stable and allow deterministic retry middleware.

Kai: my take: type(enum) + http_status + message + retry_hint + transient(bool) + error_id. Mapping idea: 429 -> RATE_LIMIT (retryable with retry_hint), 502/503/504 -> TRANSIENT_SERVICE (retryable), 5xx from model infra -> INTERNAL_MODEL (non-retryable, surface friendly message).

Anya: also sampleapp prints full trace to the public UI which worries me. We should show a concise human message in the app and a developer toggle to reveal full stack.

Dev-bot: created issue #4567: "standardize SDK error envelope + sampleapp UX" https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/4567

MattG: proposed PR checklist: add typed exception classes in python with attrs, create Error subclass in JS carrying fields, update sampleapp to display friendly vs dev views, unit tests for mapping 429 -> rate limit error, 502 -> transient.

Anya: tiny UX ask: include a short human_action hint like 'retry in 30s' or 'contact support with error_id' so product teams can show an actionable CTA.

Sarah-L: +1. Ensure telemetry emits error_id and code so SRE can correlate logs without exposing PII.

Kai: I'll implement the python exceptions and update backend logging in sampleapp. Matt, can you own the js client shim? I'll file the issue and assign.

MattG: yep, I'll handle the JS side and add tests. aiming for PRs by end of day PST.

Anya: thanks team :rocket:
